facts.raw_span: A 2-month-old full-term female
known complex congenital heart disease
single ventricle defect, double-outlet right ventricle with D-transposition of the great arteries, and an ostium secundum atrial septal defect with left superior vena cava
admitted for evaluation of occasional cyanosis
oxygen saturation of 80%
showed no signs of respiratory distress
medications included furosemide and spironolactone
became hemodynamically unstable and suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest requiring cardiac massage
cardiac catheterization was performed via the left femoral artery
nonionic iodinated contrast (Iopromide) totaling 3 mL/kg over 30 minutes
clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions
noncontrast head CT showed a slight diffuse increase in cortical density predominantly in the right frontal, parietal, and occipital lobes

concepts.why: The patient has a known complex congenital heart disease with specific defects.
The patient developed seizures and had a noncontrast head CT showing a slight diffuse increase in cortical density after a cardiorespiratory arrest.
The patient received nonionic iodinated contrast during cardiac catheterization, which may cause contrast-induced nephropathy.
The patient became hemodynamically unstable and suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest during the procedure.
The patient developed clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions, indicating a seizure disorder.
The patient had a noncontrast head CT showing a slight diffuse increase in cortical density, indicating cerebral edema.
The patient was admitted for evaluation of occasional cyanosis and had an oxygen saturation of 80%.
The patient has a complex congenital heart disease with neurological and renal implications, indicating a multisystem disorder.

rationales.F08: Cardiorespiratory arrest is a strong indicator of C04 and a moderate indicator of C02.
rationales.F11: Clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions are strong indicators of C05.
rationales.F12: Noncontrast head CT showing a slight diffuse increase in cortical density is a strong indicator of C02 and C06.
